host.platform: single-host Linux VM (Debian 13) — Caddy reverse proxy :81 → app :3000, Node 24 / Bun 1.3 / Python 3.12
host.app_server: Next.js dev server (bun run dev) under scripts/server_supervisor.sh (self-healing, 20s poll)

workers.model: host-supervisor (python task107/108 pipeline) — singleton locks + idempotency ledger

host.scheduler: host supervisor (python task107/108 pipeline) + GitHub Actions workflows (daily-psx-pipeline, intraday-poll, browser-tests, production-build)
host.rollback: scripts/start_server.sh restores the full app after a host recycle; git origin/main holds the last released commit; db/backups/*.db hold pre-migration snapshots

capacity_assessment.memory_pressure: available 885MB of 4041MB — SINGLE-CONSTRAINED HOST: no Redis provisioning (see decision), dev server + worker must stay the only long-lived processes

evidence: Only ~166-757MB RAM free under current load (Next dev + Python pipeline + Caddy); a Redis process + its fork overhead risks OOM-killing the app or worker — exactly the 'jeopardize the existing host' case Part F forbids.
All durable guarantees (worker singleton locks, idempotency ledgers, prediction history, beta profiles/invites) already live in SQLite — durable state does NOT depend on Redis.
Cache consumers (signals, patterns, dividends, LLM overlays) are read-through caches: a miss recomputes from verified DB data — degraded mode costs latency, not correctness.
Single-process deployment makes the Task 117 in-process rate limiter sound; multi-instance deployment is NOT supported by design and is documented as such.
redis_decision.revisit_when: host RAM upgrade, or a real multi-instance deployment, or cross-process rate limiting becomes necessary
redis_decision.degraded_guarantees: cache: none (recompute per request); rate limiting: per-process, resets on restart (abuse protection only, never correctness); worker locks/idempotency: FULL (SQLite, unaffected)
